section: Section II: Objectives, Eligible Projects, and Benef
text: DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE AGRICULTURE INFRASTRUCTURE FUND (AIF) GUIDELINES 2025 Chapter II: Objectives, Eligible Projects, and Beneficiaries Norm 4: Eligible Post-Harvest Management Projects Under AIF, medium-to-long term debt financing is provided for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets, including: 1. Modern Cold Storage and Cold Chain facilities. 2. Warehouses, Silos, and Pack-houses. 3. Sorting, Grading, and Primary Processing units. 4. E-marketing platforms tied to e-NAM and assaying labs. Eligible beneficiaries include Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Marketing Cooperative Societies, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self Help Groups (SHGs), and individual Agri-entrepreneurs.

section: Section IV: Financial Incentives, Interest Subventio
text: Chapter IV: Financial Incentives, Interest Subvention, and Moratorium Norm 7: Interest Subvention Structure All loans disbursed under this financing facility shall have an interest subvention of 3.0% per annum up to a loan limit of Rs. 2.00 Crore (Rupees Two Crore). In case of loans sanctioned to PACS, the interest subvention is directly passed on to reduce borrowing rates to below 4% per annum. Norm 9: Maximum Duration of Subvention The interest subvention benefit is available for a maximum period of 7 years from the date of first loan disbursement. Norm 11: Credit Guarantee Coverage Credit guarantee coverage under the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) scheme is available for loans up to Rs. 2.00 Crore. The guarantee fee shall be paid entirely by the Central Government without burdening the borrowing PACS or farmer.

section: Section II: Target Beneficiaries and Eligibility Nor
text: RESERVE BANK OF INDIA & NABARD GUIDELINES KISAN CREDIT CARD (KCC) AND INTEREST SUBVENTION NORMS Chapter II: Target Beneficiaries and Eligibility Norm 3: Eligible Categories of Borrowers 1. All farmers — individual or joint borrowers who are owner-cultivators. 2. Tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers cultivating leased agricultural land. 3. Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers including tenant farmers. 4. Beneficiaries undertaking allied agricultural activities: Dairy, Fishery, Poultry, and Animal Husbandry. No collateral security or mortgage of agricultural land is required for crop loans sanctioned up to Rs. 1,60,000/-.

section: Section III: Credit Limit Determination and Scale of
text: Chapter III: Credit Limit Determination and Scale of Finance Norm 6: Assessment of Scale of Finance The credit limit under Kisan Credit Card for the first year is fixed based on: a) Cultivated acreage multiplied by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) Scale of Finance for each crop. b) Plus 10% of limit towards post-harvest, household, and consumption requirements. c) Plus 20% of limit towards repair and maintenance expenses of farm assets plus crop insurance premium. The KCC card is valid for 5 years, with a built-in automatic 10% annual escalation in loan limit to counter inflation.

section: Section V: Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MIS
text: Chapter V: Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) Norm 12: Concessional Interest Rates and Prompt Repayment Incentive 1. The standard lending rate charged by Commercial Banks, RRBs, and Cooperative Banks for short-term crop loans is 9.0% per annum. 2. The Government of India provides an upfront Interest Subvention of 1.5% to 2.0% per annum to financial institutions. 3. Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI): An additional subvention of 3.0% per annum is provided to farmers who repay their short-term crop loans within the due date (maximum 1 year from disbursement). 4. As a result, farmers repaying on or before the due date effectively borrow at an ultra-low net interest rate of 4.0% per annum for loan limits up to Rs. 3,00,000/-. 5. In case of natural calamities where loan rescheduling is sanctioned, the interest subvention benefit is extended for the first year of the rescheduled term.

section: Section I: Preliminary and Definitions Rule 2: Defi
text: PRIMARY AGRICULTURAL CREDIT COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES (PACS) MODEL BY-LAWS & GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK MINISTRY OF COOPERATION Chapter I: Preliminary and Definitions Rule 2: Definitions and Operational Area 1. "Society" means the Primary Agricultural Credit Society registered under the State Cooperative Societies Act. 2. "Member" means an individual farmer or rural artisan duly admitted into membership in accordance with these By-laws. 3. "Managing Committee" means the governing body of the Society entrusted with the direction and management of affairs. 4. The area of operation of the Society shall be defined by village boundaries specified in Schedule A of the registration certificate.

section: Section III: Membership Eligibility and Shares Rule 1
text: Chapter III: Membership Eligibility and Shares Rule 14: Eligibility Criteria for Membership An individual shall be eligible for admission as an ordinary member of the Society if he/she satisfies all of the following conditions: a) Is a citizen of India and has attained 18 years of age. b) Is of sound mind and not an undischarged insolvent. c) Has agricultural land holdings, is an operational tenant farmer, or pursues allied agricultural activities within the operational area of the Society. d) Has purchased at least one full share valued at Rs. 100/- and paid the non-refundable entrance fee of Rs. 10/-. e) Has not been convicted of any offense involving moral turpitude within the preceding 5 years. No member shall be permitted to hold more than one-fifth (20%) of the total issued share capital of the Society.

section: Section IV: Voting Rights and General Body Rule 19:
text: Chapter IV: Voting Rights and General Body Rule 19: Democratic Control and Voting 1. Every ordinary member shall have exactly one vote, irrespective of the number of shares held, embodying the principle of "One Member, One Vote". 2. No member shall be allowed to vote by proxy at any meeting of the General Body. 3. Disqualification of Voting Rights: A member shall forfeit voting rights and the right to contest elections if: i) The member has defaulted on repayment of any loan or interest dues to the Society for a continuous period exceeding 12 months. ii) The member has failed to patronize the minimum business services of the Society (minimum Rs. 1,000 credit or fertilizer transaction) during the preceding financial year. iii) The member has failed to attend at least three consecutive Annual General Meetings (AGMs) without sanctioned leave.

section: Section VI: Management Committee and Board Compositi
text: Chapter VI: Management Committee and Board Composition Rule 27: Board Representation and Quorum 1. The Managing Committee shall consist of 11 elected members, of which: a) At least two seats shall be reserved for Women members. b) At least one seat shall be reserved for Scheduled Castes (SC) or Scheduled Tribes (ST) members. c) One seat shall be reserved for Small and Marginal farmers having landholding below 2 hectares. 2. The term of the Managing Committee shall be five years from the date of election. 3. The quorum for any meeting of the Managing Committee shall be one-half of the total members, or five members, whichever is higher. 4. The quorum for the Annual General Body Meeting (AGM) shall be one-third of the total voting members or 100 members, whichever is less.

section: Section VIII: Net Profit Allocation and Dividend Rules
text: Chapter VIII: Net Profit Allocation and Dividend Rules Rule 38: Disposal of Net Profits The net profits of the Society as audited by the Cooperative Department shall be allocated strictly in the following sequence: 1. Not less than 25% shall be credited to the Statutory Reserve Fund. 2. Not less than 10% shall be allocated to the Bad and Doubtful Debt Fund. 3. A contribution of 1% to the Cooperative Education Fund maintained by the State Cooperative Union. 4. The maximum dividend payable to ordinary members on their paid-up share capital shall not exceed 15% per annum, subject to the prior written approval of the Registrar of Cooperative Societies.

section: Section 1: Establishment of Grievance Redressal Mec
text: COOPERATIVE GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL PROTOCOL & CITIZEN CHARTER NATIONAL FEDERATION OF COOPERATIVES & STATE DEPT OF COOPERATION Section 1: Establishment of Grievance Redressal Mechanism Every Primary Agricultural Credit Society (PACS) and District Central Cooperative Bank (DCCB) is mandated to establish an Internal Grievance Redressal Cell. The Secretary of the Society shall act as the First Nodal Grievance Officer, assisted by an elected member of the Managing Committee who is not an office-bearer. A dedicated complaint register must be displayed openly at the society counter, and all complaints received digitally or physically must be logged without exception.

section: Section 3: Grievance Submission and Tracking System
text: Section 3: Grievance Submission and Tracking System Clause 3.1: Lodging Complaints and Unique Identifier 1. Any member or beneficiary farmer may register a grievance regarding: a) Delay or arbitrary denial of crop insurance claims or documentation. b) Irregularities in fertilizer/seed distribution or credit disbursement. c) Non-issuance of share certificates or refusal of membership admission. d) Unaccounted deductions from bank accounts or passbook discrepancy. 2. Every grievance must be officially acknowledged within 3 working days with a timestamped receipt. 3. A unique tracking identifier formatted as GRV-YYYY-XXXXX (e.g. GRV-2026-00101) shall be assigned and communicated to the complainant via SMS/digital receipt.

section: Section 5: Resolution Timelines and Three-Tier Esca
text: Section 5: Resolution Timelines and Three-Tier Escalation Matrix Clause 5.2: Three-Tier Escalation Hierarchy Tier 1 — Society Level (PACS): The Society Nodal Officer must investigate and resolve the grievance within 15 calendar days from the date of receipt. Tier 2 — District Level (Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies): If the grievance is not resolved within 15 days, or if the complainant is dissatisfied with the decision of the Society, the matter shall be automatically or manually escalated to the District Deputy Registrar. The Deputy Registrar shall conduct a hearing and pass a reasoned speaking order within 30 calendar days. Tier 3 — State Level (Cooperative Ombudsman / Tribunal): In cases involving financial disputes exceeding Rs. 50,000 or allegations of systemic corruption, an appeal lies before the State Cooperative Ombudsman, whose binding order shall be issued within 45 days.

section: Section 8: Accountability, Penalties, and Whistlebl
text: Section 8: Accountability, Penalties, and Whistleblower Protection Where an officer of the Cooperative Society is found guilty of willful negligence, malicious suppression of insurance documents, or unreasonable delay beyond prescribed timelines: 1. The Deputy Registrar may order compensatory damages up to Rs. 5,000 to be paid to the aggrieved farmer from the Society's administrative expense fund. 2. The Society may recover such penalty directly from the defaulting employee's salary. 3. Complainants filing bona fide grievances are protected against retaliatory denial of agricultural credit or inputs under Section 42 of the Cooperative Vigilance Regulations.

section: Section 1: Scheme Objectives and Coverage Scope The
text: MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA (PMFBY) OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES - 2024 REVISION Section 1: Scheme Objectives and Coverage Scope The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) aims at supporting sustainable production in agriculture sector by way of: a) Providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen events. b) Stabilizing the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming. c) Encouraging farmers to adopt innovative and modern agricultural practices. d) Ensuring flow of credit to the agriculture sector. The scheme covers all Food & Oilseeds crops and Annual Commercial / Annual Horticultural crops for which past yield data based on Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) is available. All farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing the notified crops in the notified area are eligible for coverage.

section: Section 4: Premium Rates and Subsidy Structure Clau
text: Section 4: Premium Rates and Subsidy Structure Clause 4.1: Maximum Premium Payable by Farmers The actuarial premium rate shall be subsidized jointly by the Central Government and State Governments. The maximum premium rate payable by the farmer shall be as follows: 1. Kharif Season (All Food grain & Oilseeds crops): Maximum 2.0% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less. 2. Rabi Season (All Food grain & Oilseeds crops): Maximum 1.5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less. 3. Annual Commercial and Annual Horticultural crops: Maximum 5.0% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less. The balance premium beyond the farmer's share is paid by the Central and State Governments on a 50:50 sharing basis, except in North Eastern states where the sharing pattern is 90:10.

section: Section 7: Mid-Season Adversity Relief Clause 7
text: Section 7: Mid-Season Adversity Relief Clause 7.2: Immediate Relief in Case of Natural Calamities In case of adverse seasonal conditions during the crop season such as severe drought, dry spells, unseasonal rains, or floods, where the expected yield during the season is likely to be less than 50% of the normal yield: a) Immediate on-account payment up to 25% of likely claims will be released to eligible farmers. b) The adversity must be notified by the State Government through a joint committee assessment comprising the District Agriculture Officer and Insurance Company representative within 7 days of occurrence. c) The on-account payment shall be adjusted against the final claim settlement upon completion of Crop Cutting Experiments.

section: Section 11: Localized Calamities & Claim Settlement
text: Section 11: Localized Calamities & Claim Settlement Procedure Clause 11.1: Loss Assessment for Localized Calamities Localized risks covered under the scheme are Hailstorm, Landslide, Inundation, Cloud burst, and Natural Fire due to lightning. Mandatory Claim Intimation Procedure: 1. The insured farmer must notify the Insurance Company, Local Agriculture Department official, or PACS within 72 hours of the occurrence of the localized calamity. 2. Intimation can be submitted via the National Crop Insurance Portal (NCIP), Crop Insurance Mobile App, or Toll-Free Kisan Call Centre (1800-180-1551). 3. The intimation must contain the farmer's name, survey number, crop name, estimated percentage loss, and bank account details. 4. An appointed loss assessor or surveyor must be deputed within 48 hours of intimation. 5. The joint field assessment must be completed within 10 days, and the claim compensation must be credited directly to the farmer's Aadhaar-linked bank account (DBT) within 15 days of survey completion.

section: Section 14: General Exclusions from Risk Coverage Th
text: Section 14: General Exclusions from Risk Coverage The insurance company shall not be liable for compensation under the following conditions: a) Losses arising from war, invasion, civil rebellion, or nuclear risks. b) Malicious damage, theft, or intentional destruction of harvested produce. c) Losses caused by preventable domestic or wild animal grazing, unless specifically notified by the State Government as an add-on cover. d) Post-harvest losses occurring beyond 14 days from harvesting, or losses to produce stored in godowns/threshing yards not left in cut and spread condition in the field.
